course_summary:
ISEN 631 | Cognitive Systems Engineering | Spring 2026
Instructor: Thomas Ferris | tferris@tamu.edu
Grading: Reading responses and Discussion board [20%], Exams: midterm [25%], Exams: final exam [25%], Semester project deliverables [30%] — A: 90-100% B: 80-89% C: 70-79% D: 60-69% F: 59% and lower
Topics: Skill-Rule-Knowledge Framework, Human error models, Bridging the Gulfs of Execution and Evaluation, Ecological Interface Design, NICU incubator design, dynamic fault management, ironies of automation, Trust in human-automation systems, Human-automation interaction models, Design-induced error, error management techniques, Resilience Engineering principles, formal task analytical methodologies, qualitative data collection, in situ data collection, front end analysis, system design strategies, human behavioral modes, interactions of humans and other system elements, sociotechnical systems engineering, current trends in CSE research, historical foundations, cognitive work, joint human-machine systems, user-centered design techniques, human-centered design methods, human-centered redesign solutions, Task analysis, Cognitive Task Analysis, system tasks/functions, subtasks identification, system breakdowns identification, system improvements proposal, solution design, solution evaluation, usability study, focus groups, interviews, surveys, mini-experiments, Project proposal, sociotechnical system definition/modeling, technology development, software tool, external memory aid, information visualization, procedural change, training method, Display/interface principles, Display/interface design, usability, Decision Making models, human tendencies, Decision Support Systems, Emotion factors, Stress factors, artifacts, displays, social interaction, stress, time pressure, competing demands, uncertainty, human cognitive functions, perception, attention, memory, decision-making, problem-solving, communication, planning, analysis methods, design methods, research methods, evaluation methods, underlying theory, creativity skills, communication skills
Tools: Canvas, Discussion Boards
Prerequisites: ISEN 635, ISEN 430/ISEN 630, or approval of instructor

headers.text: A. An insightful question about the reading. Time permitting, I will address as many of these questions as I can in lecture, and classmates will have a chance to respond as well.
B. A comment about how the reading relates to other course concepts or to an example/anecdote from your own life experience.
